newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee firm brings prices, costs into line.
newsitem.headline: German coffee firm brings prices, costs into line.

text.p: Germany's coffee market leader Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS) will bring its roasted coffee prices more closely into line with raw material costs, a company spokesman said.
It will shorten the notice period for changes in prices charged to wholesalers and restrict sales of discounted volumes, Rolf Sauerbier said on Tuesday.
"We used to allow up to three months before price increases were implemented," he told a news conference. "We're now down to a fortnight and are looking to shorten this period."
Sauerbier said green coffee prices should stay volatile throughout 1997 and 1998.

KJS, which accounted for 35.5 percent of German roasted coffee sales in March, said roasters had raised prices by up to 2.50 marks per 500 grams since March but consumers were paying only an additional 0.50 marks on average.
This was because of earlier hoarding by retailers, some of which were selling at a loss.
While this was good for consumption in the short term, sharp losses in coffee sales might follow later this year.
KJS, which plans further price rises in June, is part of Philip Morris.
